evidence.quote:
he had made a mirror with the power of causing all that was good and
      beautiful when it was reflected therein, to look poor and mean; but that
      which was good-for-nothing and looked ugly was shown magnified and
      increased in ugliness
evidence.paraphrase: A magic mirror is described as distorting reflections so good things look ugly and ugly things look worse.

evidence.quote:
the mirror shook so terribly with grinning, that it flew out of
      their hands and fell to the earth, where it was dashed in a hundred
      million and more pieces
evidence.paraphrase: The magic mirror shatters into millions of pieces that scatter across the world.

evidence.quote:
when they got into people's eyes, there
      they stayed; and then people saw everything perverted, or only had an eye
      for that which was evil. This happened because the very smallest bit had
      the same power which the whole mirror had possessed. Some persons even got
      a splinter in their heart, and then it made one shudder, for their heart
      became like a lump of ice.
evidence.paraphrase: The mirror fragments retain the whole mirror's distorting power and, lodged in eyes or hearts, corrupt people's perception or freeze their feelings.

evidence.quote:
It was just one of those
      pieces of glass from the magic mirror that had got into his eye; and poor
      Kay had got another piece right in his heart. It will soon become like
      ice.
evidence.paraphrase: Kay is transformed after mirror fragments enter his eye and heart, foreshadowing his heart turning to ice.

evidence.quote:
that rose is cankered! And
      look, this one is quite crooked! After all, these roses are very ugly!
evidence.paraphrase: Kay reacts to the mirror splinter by suddenly seeing beauty as ugliness and becoming cruel.

evidence.quote:
The flake of snow grew larger and larger; and at last it was like a young
      lady, dressed in the finest white gauze, made of a million little flakes
      like stars. She was so beautiful and delicate, but she was of ice, of
      dazzling, sparkling ice; yet she lived
evidence.paraphrase: A snowflake enlarges and becomes the living Snow Queen, a being made of ice.

evidence.quote:
on she flew with him; flew high over
      the black clouds, while the storm moaned and whistled as though it were
      singing some old tune. On they flew over woods and lakes, over seas, and
      many lands
evidence.paraphrase: The Snow Queen carries Kay away by flight over great distances of land and sea.

evidence.quote:
then he forgot little Gerda, grandmother, and all whom he had left at
      his home
evidence.paraphrase: After the Snow Queen's kiss, Kay forgets his former life and companions.

evidence.quote:
her hot tears fell just
      where a rose-bush had sunk; and when her warm tears watered the ground,
      the tree shot up suddenly as fresh and blooming as when it had been
      swallowed up
evidence.paraphrase: Gerda's tears cause a hidden rose-bush to spring up again from the ground.

evidence.quote:
you can, I know, twist all the
      winds of the world together in a knot. If the seaman loosens one knot,
      then he has a good wind; if a second, then it blows pretty stiffly; if he
      undoes the third and fourth, then it rages so that the forests are
      upturned.
evidence.paraphrase: The Reindeer describes the Finland woman's power to control winds by binding them in knots that release different wind strengths.

evidence.quote:
the reason of that is, he has a splinter of glass in his eye, and in his
      heart. These must be got out first; otherwise he will never go back to
      mankind, and the Snow Queen will retain her power over him.
evidence.paraphrase: The Finland woman explains that Kay's captivity is caused by glass splinters that must be removed to free him.

evidence.quote:
There then came a whole regiment of
      snow-flakes, but they did not fall from above, and they were quite bright
      and shining from the Aurora Borealis. The flakes ran along the ground, and
      the nearer they came the larger they grew.
evidence.paraphrase: Living snowflakes serving as the Snow Queen's outposts move along the ground and grow, taking monstrous shapes.

evidence.quote:
The cold was so intense that she
      could see her own breath, which came like smoke out of her mouth. It grew
      thicker and thicker, and took the form of little angels
evidence.paraphrase: Gerda's breath transforms into an army of angels that defend her against the snowflakes.

evidence.quote:
they penetrated to his heart, they
      thawed the lumps of ice, and consumed the splinters of the looking-glass
evidence.paraphrase: Gerda's tears melt the ice in Kay's heart and destroy the mirror splinters, reversing his transformation.

evidence.quote:
the splinter rolled
      out of his eye, and he recognised her, and shouted, "Gerda, sweet little
      Gerda! Where have you been so long? And where have I been?"
evidence.paraphrase: Once the splinter is expelled, Kay weeps, recognizes Gerda, and returns to his former self.

evidence.quote:
as they entered, they
      remarked that they were now grown up
evidence.paraphrase: On returning home, Kay and Gerda find that they have grown up during their long absence.
